root_cause.text: In `net/sctp/input.c::__sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup()`, the SCTP ASCONF lookup path only validated the fixed ADDIP/parameter header size and failed to verify that the entire variable-length address parameter fit within the chunk before calling `af->from_addr_param()`, allowing truncated ASCONF data to be read as uninitialized memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) > ntohs(ch->length)) return NULL;` with the comment that “the whole address parameter must lie within the chunk before `af->from_addr_param()` reads the variable-length address; otherwise a truncated trailing ASCONF chunk lets it read uninitialized bytes past the parameter,” and the CVE description says the function “only checks that the ASCONF chunk can hold the ADDIP header and a parameter header, then calls `af->from_addr_param()`, which reads the full address ... trusting the parameter's declared length.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `net/sctp/input.c::__sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup()`, the SCTP ASCONF lookup path only validated the fixed ADDIP/parameter header size and failed to verify that the entire variable-length address parameter fit within the chunk before calling `af->from_addr_param()`, allowing truncated ASCONF data to be read as uninitialized memory.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds a bounds check `if (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) > ntohs(ch->length)) return NULL;` with the comment that “the whole address parameter must lie within the chunk before `af->from_addr_param()` reads the variable-length address; otherwise a truncated trailing ASCONF chunk lets it read uninitialized bytes past the parameter,” and the CVE description says the function “only checks that the ASCONF chunk can hold the ADDIP header and a parameter header, then calls `af->from_addr_param()`, which reads the full address ... trusting the parameter's declared length.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length validation to reject truncated ASCONF address parameters before parsing them.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added in __sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup() after locating the ASCONF address parameter: the code now verifies that sizeof(*asconf) plus the parameter length does not exceed the chunk length, and returns NULL if it does, before calling sctp_get_af_specific() and af->from_addr_param().
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents parsing a truncated ASCONF chunk whose address parameter extends beyond the received chunk, avoiding reads of uninitialized or out-of-bounds bytes when the variable-length address is decoded.

grouping_result.intent: Add a length validation to reject truncated ASCONF address parameters before parsing them.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause by adding a length check to prevent truncated ASCONF address parameters from being parsed, which addresses the missing bounds validation in the SCTP ASCONF lookup path.

candidates.rationale: This computes a pointer directly to the variable-length address parameter without any preceding bounds check against the ASCONF chunk length, enabling later parsing of truncated data.

This dereferences the parameter type from the potentially truncated address parameter before verifying the full parameter is present, contributing to out-of-bounds/uninitialized reads in the lookup path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This advances directly to the variable-length address parameter inside the ASCONF chunk without first verifying that the full parameter fits in the received chunk, which is the root cause of the truncated-ASCONF read.
This reads the parameter type from the potentially truncated address parameter before any complete length validation, allowing later parsing to operate on uninitialized or out-of-bounds data.
